subject: [PATCH v5 04/19] selftests/mm: skip khugepaged page cache cases without a PMD folio

2026-09-08.patch_summary: This patch modifies the selftests/mm module to skip khugepaged page cache cases that do not support PMD folios. The issue arises from a limitation in the page cache, which caps folio order at MAX_PAGECACHE_ORDER, below the PMD order on certain architectures. As a result, the kernel refuses collapses for PMD-sized pages, leading to test failures. To address this, the patch introduces a new function thp_file_supported_orders() to determine supported orders and skips shmem and file mem types where the cap is below the PMD order. This ensures that tests are only run on architectures that support PMD folios.

reviews.author: Baolin Wang
reviews.summary: Approved the patch, adding a Reviewed-by tag.
reviews.raw_body:
On 9/8/26 8:50 PM, Kiryl Shutsemau wrote:
> From: "Kiryl Shutsemau (Meta)" <kas@kernel.org>
> 
> The page cache caps folio order at MAX_PAGECACHE_ORDER, which is below the
> PMD order on arm64 with 64K pages, where a PMD is 512M.  A PMD-sized page
> cache folio is impossible there, so the kernel refuses these collapses:
> MADV_COLLAPSE answers -EINVAL and khugepaged passes over the range.  Four
> shmem cases ask for a PMD-sized folio anyway, fail, and the run bails out
> in the middle.
> 
> Skip the shmem and file mem types where the cap is below the PMD order.
> 
> The cap is not shmem-specific: it applies to every file folio.  Add
> thp_file_supported_orders() to read the orders the page cache allows.
> 
> Anonymous collapse is unaffected: its orders are not capped this way.
> 
> Assisted-by: LLM
> Reviewed-by: Mike Rapoport (Microsoft) <rppt@kernel.org>
> Tested-by: Muhammad Usama Anjum <usama.anjum@arm.com>
> Signed-off-by: Kiryl Shutsemau (Meta) <kas@kernel.org>
> ---

LGTM.
Reviewed-by: Baolin Wang <baolin.wang@linux.alibaba.com>

2026-09-09.patch_summary: This patch series introduces a new function, thp_file_supported_orders(), to determine the supported page cache orders for regular files. It then uses this information in selftests/mm/khugepaged.c to skip khugepaged page cache cases where a PMD-sized folio is not possible due to the page cache order cap.
